sub_sections.title: Quality and effectiveness of the work plan, assessment of risks and appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages
sub_sections.content:
## 3.1 Quality and effectiveness of the work plan, assessment of risks and appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages

### Overall structure of the work plan

FIELDWISE is a single-beneficiary MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship: Dr. Rositsa Cholakova is recruited by and hosted at HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont (ATK) in Martonvásár, Hungary, under primary supervision by Dr. Roland Hollós (ATK) and co-supervision by Prof. András Jung at the associated partner Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE). It is a European Fellowship of 30 months: a 24-month research fellowship at HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont (M1-M24) followed by a six-month non-academic placement at AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság (M25-M30). There is no separate secondment; the placement is the inter-sectoral mobility element and is shown on the Gantt chart.

The work plan is organised into five work packages that follow the scientific logic of the objectives from raw evidence to operational uptake, so that each work package consumes a validated output of its predecessor rather than running in parallel silos:

- WP1 - Data Harmonisation and Physiological Stress Definition (lead: HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont) delivers objective O1: it harmonises the heterogeneous 2022-2026 processing-tomato archive of Magyar Agrár- és Élettudományi Egyetem (MATE) into a QC-controlled common-variable matrix and fixes a physiologically meaningful water-stress target and a pre-registered validation protocol.
- WP2 - HUN-REN Modelling and ELTE Scale Harmonisation (lead: HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont) delivers objective O2: it builds a parsimonious, interpretable, uncertainty-aware primary water-status model with one nonlinear benchmark where justified, separates reusable system components from crop-specific parameters, and defines the spectral/UAV/Sentinel scaling and crop-transfer specification.
- WP3 - Independent Commercial-Farmer Prospective Validation (lead: the independent commercial-farmer validation site) delivers objective O3: it instruments an independent commercial field and measures the transfer gap of the historical model prospectively, with uncertainty and any limited recalibration stated openly.
- WP4 - DrR Web MVP, Co-development and Exploitation Preparation (lead: КРУМАТИК ЕООД) delivers objective O4's build strand: it co-develops a crop-configurable DrR web MVP carrying the validated processing-tomato module and prepares the exploitation route and the placement evaluation protocol, using structured AgroVIR requirements consultation from M1.
- WP5 - AgroVIR Non-Academic Placement (lead: AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság) delivers objective O4's evaluation strand: during the M25-M30 placement it evaluates the MVP operationally within a real farm-management-information-system environment and defines the post-MSCA integration and exploitation roadmap.

The plan carries eleven deliverables and five milestones. The deliverables are: D1.1 Harmonised database/metadata and variable-availability map (M6), D1.2 Stress-target, feature-selection and validation protocol (M6), D1.3 Career Development Plan (M3); D2.1 Primary model, benchmark and model card (M14), D2.2 Spectral/UAV/Sentinel harmonisation, scaling and crop-transfer specification (M14); D3.1 Independent commercial-field validation dataset (M18), D3.2 Prospective transferability, uncertainty and limited-recalibration report (M18); D4.1 Crop-configurable DrR web MVP with validated processing-tomato module (M24), D4.2 Pre-placement technical/usability requirements dossier (M24); D5.1 AgroVIR operational/interoperability assessment (M30), D5.2 Post-MSCA FMIS integration and exploitation roadmap (M30). The Career Development Plan (D1.3) is front-loaded to M3 so that the training and career logic frames the whole fellowship, and is reviewed at each steering point.

The five milestones are decision gates rather than restatements of deliverables, each carrying a verifiable achievement criterion: MS1 Historical knowledge base and target definition complete (M6); MS2 Model and scale-transition framework ready for final prospective assessment (M14); MS3 Independent real-world transferability quantified (M18); MS4 MVP ready for industrial placement evaluation (M24); MS5 Industrial evaluation and placement completed (M30). MS4 is the pivotal gate: only a validated, externally-access-tested MVP passes into the industrial placement, so that the M25-M30 placement is never spent stabilising an immature tool. MS5 falls in the placement's last month, so the placement window is milestoned by construction and its completion is evidenced directly by D5.1 and D5.2.

### Timing of the work packages and their components, and the critical path

The timeline fits comfortably within the 30-month duration. The confirmed schedule places WP1 in M1-M6, WP2 in M3-M14, WP3 in M4-M18, WP4 in M1-M24 and WP5 in M25-M30. Three design choices give the plan its robustness. First, WP4 runs continuously from M1 to M24: software co-development with КРУМАТИК ЕООД and AgroVIR requirements consultation (T4.4) begin at the outset rather than waiting for the science to finish, so the MVP integrates validated functions incrementally instead of in a risky end-load. Second, the field-dependent tasks of WP3 (installation T3.2 in M5-M7; coordinated physiological, proximal and thermal campaigns T3.3 in M7-M14; UAV and Sentinel acquisition T3.4 in M8-M15) are positioned to catch the growing season, and the securing of written field access (T3.1) is scheduled in M4-M6, well ahead of instrumentation. Third, the two temporally strict, finish-to-start couplings are honoured with slack: WP4 ends at M24 before WP5 starts at M25, and the migration of validated core functions (T4.3, M18-M22) precedes the placement evaluation (T5.1, M25-M27).

The critical path runs T1.3 (select the primary physiological stress target) -> T2.2 (develop the parsimonious primary model and benchmark) -> T3.5 (apply the historical model prospectively and quantify the transfer gap) -> T4.3 (migrate validated core functions toward the MVP) -> T5.1 (operational evaluation at AgroVIR). This is exactly the scientific spine of the proposal - target definition, modelling, prospective validation, productisation, industrial evaluation - which means the schedule protects the highest-value chain of work. The inter-WP dependencies are explicit: WP1 feeds WP2 and WP3 (the common-variable matrix, the stress target and the pre-registered protocol govern both), WP2 feeds WP3 (T3.5 applies the WP2 historical model prospectively) and WP4 (T4.2 implements the WP2 reusable/crop-specific separation), WP3 feeds WP4 (only the WP3-validated module migrates into D4.1), and WP4 gates WP5 through the MS4 MVP-ready check. The dependency graph is acyclic and no critical-path dependency is left unresolved.

### Appropriateness of the effort assigned to work packages

The fellow's 30 person-months are distributed to match where the intellectual load lies: WP1 3.0 PM, WP2 6.0 PM, WP3 6.6 PM, WP4 6.0 PM, WP5 5.4 PM, and 3.0 PM cross-cutting (supervision cadence, training, open-science and reporting), totalling 30.0 PM. The weighting is science-heavy and honest: the two most demanding and most novel strands - modelling (WP2) and the independent prospective validation with its field campaigns (WP3) - together take almost half the fellow's time, while WP1 is deliberately lean because it reuses an existing archive rather than mounting a new data campaign. The build (WP4) and the industrial placement (WP5) are resourced enough to deliver a working MVP and a substantive operational evaluation without displacing the research core.

The fellow's effort is complemented by partner in-kind contributions that are stated as operator-declared estimates pending written partner confirmation: approximately 2.5 PM from the ATK supervisor, 2.0 PM from the ELTE co-supervisor, 3.0 PM from AgroVIR (the only partner hosting the fellow, and correspondingly the largest partner figure), 2.4 PM from MATE and 1.5 PM from КРУМАТИК ЕООД. These figures were built bottom-up from the accepted governance cadence and role descriptions and are to be verified with each partner before the grant; they are presented here as declared assumptions, not as confirmed commitments.

### Mechanisms to assess and mitigate risks

The project carries a ten-row risk register spanning research and administrative risks, each with a likelihood (L/M/H), impact (L/M/H) and a concrete mitigation, and it is anchored by an explicit risk philosophy: a drop in prospective performance is treated as a scientific result to be quantified with stated uncertainty and addressed by limited, transparent recalibration, never hidden. The register is:

- R01 Historical MATE variables differ among years (L=M, I=H): use an explicit year-by-variable matrix; harmonise only defensible common variables; retain year-specific measurements as secondary information.
- R02 Effective biological sample size is limited (L=M, I=H): use repeated-measure/hierarchical structure, conservative feature reduction and parsimonious modelling; no deep-learning dependency.
- R03 Farmer site lacks modern monitoring infrastructure (L=H, I=M): install a project meteorological station and soil sensors before the validation campaign; define maintenance and data-quality responsibilities.
- R04 Primary farmer access changes or is interrupted (L=M, I=H): secure written access; maintain the Szentendre Skanzen model-garden route as a contingency subject to formal agreement and scientific suitability.
- R05 ELTE instrument access or timing is constrained (L=M, I=H): use a written equipment/operation schedule; prioritise key physiological dates; retain physiology/proximal sensing as the core pathway if individual UAV campaigns are missed.
- R06 Field geometry or clouds limit Sentinel-2 interpretation (L=H, I=M): use Sentinel only where valid pixels support field-scale inference; rely on UAV/proximal observations for finer spatial scales.
- R07 Prospective performance drops (L=M, I=H): treat transfer loss as a scientific result; quantify uncertainty and use limited transparent recalibration rather than hiding the gap.
- R08 Krumatic web development is delayed (L=M, I=M): develop incrementally from the existing desktop prototype; scientific deliverables remain primary; prioritise validated core functions over feature breadth.
- R09 AgroVIR cannot provide proprietary/customer data (L=L, I=M): design the placement around usability/interoperability requirements and protected/coded extracts; unrestricted customer-system access is not a project dependency.
- R10 MATE-derived assets have commercial restrictions (L=M, I=H): use for approved research; maintain a background/foreground inventory and conduct an institutional data-rights/IP assessment before commercial exploitation.

The register is designed so that no single point of failure can stall the fellowship. The highest-exposure external dependencies each have a pre-planned fallback that keeps the science intact: field-site loss is covered by the Szentendre Skanzen contingency (R04, and the standing T3.6 task) and by installing the project's own meteorological and soil instrumentation (R03), so the validation does not rely on pre-existing farm infrastructure; the UAV and hyperspectral campaigns run with ELTE's instruments under a written equipment schedule, and if individual flights are missed the physiology and proximal-sensing pathway remains the core route (R05, R06); software slippage is de-risked by incremental development from the existing prototype while scientific deliverables stay primary (R08); and the placement is deliberately architected to need no proprietary or customer-data access, relying on protected, coded extracts (R09), which is why its likelihood/impact is the lowest in the table. The parsimony discipline (R01, R02) directly answers the small-sample, heterogeneous-archive reality of the data.

Risk is monitored, not merely catalogued. A Project Steering Group meets at five points - M6, M14, M18, M24 and M27 - and issues a go/no-go verdict on milestones MS1-MS5; the four scheduled verdict points coincide with the milestone months so that no work package advances past a failed gate, and the retained M27 point provides a mid-placement review so the evaluated M25-M30 placement never runs unmonitored. The Career Development Plan is reviewed at the same five points. Administrative risks are handled through the same governance: the written field-access arrangement with the commercial farmer (T3.1), the MATE data-use conditions, the ELTE instrument-access schedule and the placement arrangement with AgroVIR are all being confirmed in writing before the action starts, and until they are they are carried as declared assumptions rather than as settled fact, so the plan is transparent about what remains to be closed at grant preparation.

### Gantt chart (months elapsed)

The chart below shows the work packages, major deliverables (D), milestones (MS) and the M25-M30 non-academic placement against elapsed project months 1-30. There is no secondment (European Fellowship); the placement is the mobility element shown on WP5.

```
                              1         2         3
Month (elapsed):    123456789012345678901234567890
                    ------------------------------
WP1  Data/stress    ######........................
WP2  Modelling      ..############................
WP3  Field valid.   ...###############............
WP4  DrR MVP        ########################......
WP5  Placement      ........................######
                    ------------------------------
Markers:            ..^..^.......^...^.....^.....^
                    ------------------------------
  M3  : D1.3 (Career Development Plan)
  M6  : D1.1, D1.2  | MS1 Historical knowledge base and target definition complete
  M14 : D2.1, D2.2  | MS2 Model and scale-transition framework ready for final prospective assessment
  M18 : D3.1, D3.2  | MS3 Independent real-world transferability quantified
  M24 : D4.1, D4.2  | MS4 MVP ready for industrial placement evaluation
  M30 : D5.1, D5.2  | MS5 Industrial evaluation and placement completed

Placement (non-academic, AgroVIR): M25-M30, mainly remote with monthly
  face-to-face technical reviews (WP5).
Critical path: T1.3 -> T2.2 -> T3.5 -> T4.3 -> T5.1.
```

The Gantt is included within the 10-page limit for Part B Sections 1-3 and shows months elapsed rather than calendar dates, as required. It makes the plan's logic legible at a glance: an early knowledge-base and training gate (M6), a modelling gate (M14), the decisive independent-validation gate (M18), the MVP-ready gate (M24) that admits the placement, and the closing industrial-evaluation gate (M30).

sub_sections.title: Quality and capacity of the host institutions and participating organisations, including hosting arrangements
sub_sections.content:
## 3.2 Quality and capacity of the host institutions and participating organisations, including hosting arrangements

### The host institution: HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont

FIELDWISE is a single-beneficiary MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship. The sole beneficiary, recruiting organisation and academic host is HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont (HUN-REN Centre for Agricultural Research, HUN-REN ATK), a public research organisation of the HUN-REN Hungarian Research Network, at Brunszvik u. 2, 2462 Martonvásár, Hungary. Dr. Rositsa Cholakova is recruited into its Agricultural Institute, where the primary supervisor, Dr. Roland Hollós, sits in the Department of Crop Production. The host is chosen for a precise scientific fit: it supplies the modelling and heterogeneous-data-integration environment at the core of the objectives, primary supervision by Dr. Roland Hollós (research associate, Department of Crop Production, and HUN-REN AI Ambassador for the Centre for Agricultural Research; ORCID 0000-0001-5137-7471), access to the wider HUN-REN AI and data-processing infrastructure for computationally intensive analyses, and complementary in-house plant-physiology depth through the Plant Physiology and Metabolomics Department led by Prof. Tibor Janda, whose long experience in drought and abiotic-stress physiology supports the selection and interpretation of physiological validation parameters. The computational and data-processing environment required for multi-source integration and predictive modelling is available in-house, with escalation to the shared HUN-REN research infrastructure where the workload demands it, so no dedicated hardware needs to be provisioned.

HUN-REN ATK is a proven MSCA host. It coordinated and hosted the funded MSCA Individual Fellowship LANDRACES (H2020 grant 752453, MSCA-IF-EF-ST Standard European Fellowship, 2017-2019), evidencing that the beneficiary already possesses the institutional machinery — recruitment, supervision, financial administration and researcher support — that an MSCA-PF requires. Its research standing in the exact methods FIELDWISE relies on is documented: the supervisor's own modelling line (Hollós et al. 2026, on the Biome-BGC model, Geoscientific Model Development) and current Horizon participations verified on CORDIS (COUSIN, AI4SoilHealth, TUdi). Because ATK is a research organisation rather than a university, the fellowship's teaching and outreach exposure is routed deliberately through guest lectures, seminars and practical sessions at MATE and, where institutionally possible, the Agricultural University of Plovdiv, rather than being claimed as an in-house degree-teaching load the host cannot offer.

### Hosting arrangements, integration and support services

The host provides the fellow with a workspace at the Agricultural Institute in Martonvásár, integration into the supervisor's hosting group, administrative and grants support, access to training, and continuation of these arrangements throughout the M25-M30 non-academic placement so that the fellow is not administratively cut adrift during the inter-sectoral phase. Integration into the team is reinforced by the supervision cadence described in Section 3.1 — a weekly one-to-one with the supervisor, a monthly written progress record and quarterly Career Development Plan reviews — which embeds the fellow in the day-to-day scientific life of the Department of Crop Production and, through Prof. Tibor Janda's department, in the institute's physiology environment. Dr. Roland Hollós accepts the primary-supervisor role and carries the modelling-intensive supervision. These hosting arrangements and support services, and the supervisor's formal acceptance, are the beneficiary's own facilities and commitments; they are stated here as the operator's declared position and will be confirmed in ATK's written hosting statement (naming the Part A signatory and the grants-office contact) at grant preparation, rather than presented as already-settled fact.

### The non-academic placement host: AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság

The inter-sectoral mobility element of this European Fellowship is a six-month non-academic placement (M25-M30) at AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság (AGROVIR Kft.), a Hungarian SME founded in 2007 and seated in Budaörs that develops and operates a cloud-based farm-management information system (FMIS). AgroVIR is the operational evaluator: it provides structured requirements consultation from M1 through WP4 and, during the placement, the real farm-management environment in which the DrR web MVP is assessed for usability, data requirements, interoperability and future FMIS integration. Its relevance is commercial rather than academic — it reports no participation in EU-funded research projects, and its stated track record is twenty years of practice in Hungarian commercial agriculture and an FMIS in production use across more than 745,000 hectares in eight countries including Hungary and Bulgaria, the two countries FIELDWISE works in; this track-record framing is the operator's declared position pending the company's written confirmation, and is deliberately not converted into a research claim.

The placement is designed to be robust and low-dependency. It is conducted mainly through remote collaboration with monthly face-to-face technical meetings for review, feedback and progress assessment; the fellow does not require direct access to AgroVIR's proprietary software, customer databases, office infrastructure or computing equipment, and AgroVIR supplies only the information and data extracts needed for interoperability testing in protected form (coded or anonymised field identifiers such as 'Field X'). Placement supervision is provided by Miklós Maróti, Managing Director of AgroVIR, whose experience in agricultural digitalisation and farm-management systems anchors the evaluation of the MVP's stress and irrigation outputs within practical workflows, and the fellow works with the AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform. Ownership of placement results follows the grant-agreement default, vesting in HUN-REN ATK as the beneficiary acting through the fellow, with a written placement agreement between the fellow, HUN-REN ATK and AgroVIR to confirm this allocation and the access terms to the fellow's DrR background IP before the placement begins. The placement supervisor and title, the mainly-remote arrangement, the team identification, the person-month commitment and the IP allocation are the placement host's own arrangements and are carried here as the operator's declared position, to be confirmed in AgroVIR's written placement letter; no letter of commitment is submitted for a non-academic placement host, so the placement is evaluated on this Part B argument. What the placement offers that the academic host alone cannot — operational evaluation against a production FMIS, research-to-MVP translation, agricultural-software requirements practice, interoperability assessment and exploitation planning — is the inference that justifies the inter-sectoral move.

### Associated partners linked to the beneficiary

Three associated partners are linked to the beneficiary and add capacity the host does not hold in-house. Full infrastructure, logistics and facilities are detailed in Part B-2 Section 5; the essentials are as follows.

**Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE)** — Faculty of Informatics, Institute of Cartography and Geoinformatics, Budapest — supplies the remote-sensing, UAV/hyperspectral and geoinformatics environment and the co-supervisor, Prof. András Jung, who carries the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel harmonisation and scale-transition strand. ELTE's GIS and Remote Sensing Laboratory holds the project's principal spatial instruments: a DJI Matrice 350 RTK industrial drone with Zenmuse L1 (LiDAR/RGB), P1 (45 MP photogrammetry) and H20T (thermal) payloads, an Ultris S5 hyperspectral camera and a Cubert CUVIS laboratory hyperspectral package, together with licensed ArcGIS, ENVI and MATLAB, open geospatial tools (Google Earth Engine, QGIS, SNAP), high-performance computing and secure storage. Practical UAV operations are supported by Dr. Zsófia Varga (flight planning, sensor operation, data acquisition), with the fellow holding an EU A1/A3 pilot licence. The instrument inventory and ELTE's identity are confirmed; ELTE's continuation as an associated partner (rather than beneficiary), the co-supervisor's acceptance, and the written instrument-access arrangement specifying operators, sites, measurement periods and terms are carried as the operator's declared position pending ELTE's written agreement, and Section 3.1 risk R05 provides the constrained-access fallback.

**Magyar Agrár- és Élettudományi Egyetem (MATE)** — Institute of Horticultural Sciences — is the source scientific environment. It provides the heterogeneous 2022-2026 processing-tomato archive that makes processing tomato the development crop, together with tomato plant material, trials, irrigation treatments, agronomic knowledge and the experimental/validation instrument base: TDR and capacitive soil-moisture sensors at 15 and 30 cm, stomatal resistance/conductance equipment, SPAD chlorophyll meters, VIS-NIR (approx. 325-1075 nm) and VIS-NIR-SWIR (approx. 350-2500 nm) leaf spectroradiometers, meteorological monitoring, leaf-temperature and CWSI tools. MATE's project contact is Dr. Sándor Takács, supported by precision-agriculture depth from Prof. Gábor Milics. MATE's identity, instrument base and archive description are confirmed; the contact seat and the rights and data-use conditions governing access to the archive are the operator's declared position, to be documented in MATE's written data-use permission before the action starts (see Section 3.1 risk R10 on commercial-restriction handling).

**КРУМАТИК ЕООД (Krumatic EOOD)** — a Bulgarian technology and digital-solutions company (EIK 201511899, established 2011, Sofia), whose registered manager, sole owner and signatory is Lyubomir Lyubomirov Krumov — provides continuous software-development support from project start: improving the DrR prototype, implementing the validated data/model functions and the crop-configurable architecture, migrating the validated core toward the web MVP, and later Bulgarian farmer-facing dissemination and uptake. Its role is distinct from AgroVIR's: Krumatic builds and disseminates the software vehicle, while AgroVIR evaluates the validated MVP operationally. Its legal identity, contact/signatory and role are confirmed; its SME status and its independence (its prior AgroVIR-platform deployment in Bulgaria stated openly as a commercial-deployment relationship, with no known ownership, employment or family relationship to the fellow or another partner) are the operator's declared position, and the code-IP terms for Krumatic-developed code are a pre-grant development-agreement action rather than a proposal fact.

### Collaborating validation environment and post-fellowship route

The prospective validation in WP3 is carried out at an independent commercial farmer site in Hungary, secured through the fellow's established professional relationship and deliberately kept as a collaborating validation environment rather than a beneficiary or associated partner. Because the site does not currently operate advanced monitoring infrastructure, FIELDWISE installs an automated meteorological station and soil sensors and retains responsibility for all specialised scientific measurements, while the farmer provides the field, routine crop management, agreed irrigation implementation and access for scheduled research activities. This design is the point of the exercise: the site is independent of the historical MATE experiments, so it tests whether learned relationships survive a production environment that was not used to establish them. The written field-access, sensor-installation and treatment-implementation arrangement is the operator's declared position and is obtained through task T3.1 before the campaign; site identity is collected with the arrangement, not fabricated now, and the Szentendre Skanzen model-garden route stands as a contingency-only option subject to formal agreement and scientific suitability. Beyond the fellowship, Институт по зеленчукови култури „Марица“ – Пловдив (the Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute, Bulgarian Agricultural Academy; director Prof. Daniela Ganeva) provides a confirmed post-MSCA replication, local-recalibration and extension route under Bulgarian vegetable-production conditions; it sits on no work-package month line and carries no in-action effort, so it strengthens the exploitation horizon without loading the 24-month scientific plan.

### Global Fellowship provision

FIELDWISE is a European Fellowship arising from an intra-EU move (Bulgaria to Hungary), with the six-month non-academic placement as an extension under CC-07 rather than a Global Fellowship outgoing phase. The Global Fellowship requirement to outline both an outgoing Third Country host and a return host therefore does not apply: there is no Third Country host, and the single academic host throughout is HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont.

Risk philosophy: prospective performance loss is treated as a quantified scientific result with limited transparent recalibration rather than hidden.

Project Steering Group meets at M6, M14, M18, M24 and M27, issuing go/no-go verdicts on MS1-MS5, with the M27 point a mid-placement review; CDP reviewed at the same five points.

The M25-M30 placement is conducted mainly through remote collaboration with monthly face-to-face technical meetings for review, feedback and progress assessment. The fellow works with the AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform.

The independent commercial farmer provides written field access: site availability for the validation season(s) within M4-M18, permission for sensor installation (automated meteorological station, soil sensors), field measurements and UAV campaigns, agreed irrigation-treatment implementation, and routine crop management responsibilities.

The fellow conducts or co-conducts UAV and hyperspectral measurements with ELTE's DJI Matrice 350 RTK platform (Zenmuse L1/P1/H20T) and Ultris S5 / Cubert CUVIS cameras, supported by Dr. Zsófia Varga for flight planning, sensor operation and data acquisition, scheduled around key physiological measurement dates at the validation site; ELTE software environments are available for processing.
Career Development Plan is deliverable D1.3, due M3, and is reviewed at each steering point.
HUN-REN Agrartudomanyi Kutatokozpont is the sole beneficiary, recruiting organisation and academic host, at Martonvásár, Hungary, hosting the fellow in its Agricultural Institute.
Dr. Rositsa Cholakova is the recruited experienced researcher/postdoctoral fellow.

Dr. Roland Hollós, research associate in the Department of Crop Production and HUN-REN AI Ambassador (ORCID 0000-0001-5137-7471), is the primary supervisor providing the modelling and data-integration environment.
The host provides the in-house computational/data-processing environment for multi-source integration and predictive modelling, with access to wider HUN-REN infrastructure for intensive analyses.
The Plant Physiology and Metabolomics Department led by Prof. Tibor Janda supplies complementary drought/abiotic-stress physiology depth for validation-parameter selection and interpretation.

HUN-REN ATK acts as recruiting organisation and beneficiary for the fellowship, hosting the fellow at the Agricultural Institute, Martonvásár, with workspace, integration into the hosting group, administrative support, and continuation of arrangements during the M25-M30 placement.
Dr. Roland Hollós accepts the primary-supervisor role, with weekly technical sessions through the modelling-intensive work packages and the supervision routine of the governance record.
FIELDWISE is a European Fellowship (intra-EU Bulgaria-to-Hungary move) with the six-month placement as a CC-07 extension, so the Global Fellowship outgoing/return-host requirement does not apply.
The inter-sectoral placement runs M25-M30 as the mobility element of the European Fellowship.

AGROVIR Üzletviteli Tanácsadó Korlátolt Felelősségű Társaság is a Hungarian SME founded 2007, seated in Budaörs, operating a cloud-based FMIS, acting as operational evaluator and non-academic placement host.
AgroVIR provides structured requirements consultation from M1 through WP4 and the real farm-management environment for MVP operational evaluation during the placement.

No participation in EU-funded research projects. AgroVIR's relevant track record is commercial rather than scientific: twenty years of practice in Hungarian commercial agriculture, and a farm management information system in production use across more than 745,000 hectares in eight countries, including Hungary and Bulgaria — the two countries FIELDWISE works in.

The M25-M30 placement is conducted mainly through remote collaboration with monthly face-to-face technical meetings for review, feedback and progress assessment. The fellow does not require direct access to AgroVIR's proprietary software, customer databases, office infrastructure or computing equipment; AgroVIR provides the information and data extracts required for interoperability testing in protected form (coded or anonymised field identifiers, e.g. 'Field X'). The fellow works with the AgroVIR product development team responsible for the FMIS platform.

Ownership of placement results follows the grant agreement default, vesting in HUN-REN ATK as the beneficiary acting through the fellow; a written placement agreement between the fellow, HUN-REN ATK and AgroVIR, concluded before the placement begins, will confirm this allocation and the access terms to the fellow's DrR background IP.
No letter of commitment is submitted for the non-academic placement host; the placement is evaluated on the Part B argument.

The placement offers operational evaluation against a production FMIS, research-to-MVP translation, requirements practice, interoperability assessment and exploitation planning that the academic host alone cannot provide.

Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Institute of Cartography and Geoinformatics, supplies the remote-sensing/UAV/hyperspectral/geoinformatics environment and the co-supervisor Prof. András Jung, who carries the hyperspectral-to-Sentinel harmonisation strand.

ELTE's GIS and Remote Sensing Laboratory holds the DJI Matrice 350 RTK with Zenmuse L1/P1/H20T, Ultris S5 and Cubert CUVIS cameras, plus ArcGIS/ENVI/MATLAB, open geospatial tools, HPC and secure storage.
Dr. Zsófia Varga supports practical UAV operations (flight planning, sensor operation, data acquisition); the fellow holds an EU A1/A3 pilot licence.
ELTE continues in FIELDWISE as an associated partner (not beneficiary), providing the remote-sensing/UAV/hyperspectral environment and the co-supervisor.
Prof. András Jung accepts the co-supervisor role, carrying the hyperspectral/UAV/EO harmonisation strand as a substantive methodological role.

The fellow conducts or co-conducts UAV and hyperspectral measurements with ELTE's DJI Matrice 350 RTK platform (Zenmuse L1/P1/H20T) and Ultris S5 / Cubert CUVIS cameras, supported by Dr. Zsófia Varga for flight planning, sensor operation and data acquisition, scheduled around key physiological measurement dates at the validation site; ELTE software environments are available for processing.

Magyar Agrár- és Élettudományi Egyetem (Institute of Horticultural Sciences) is the source scientific environment providing the 2022-2026 processing-tomato archive, plant material, trials, irrigation treatments and agronomic knowledge.

MATE's validation instrument base includes TDR and capacitive soil-moisture sensors at 15/30 cm, stomatal resistance/conductance equipment, SPAD meters, VIS-NIR (approx. 325-1075 nm) and VIS-NIR-SWIR (approx. 350-2500 nm) leaf spectroradiometers, meteorological monitoring, leaf-temperature and CWSI tools.
Prof. Gábor Milics provides precision-agriculture and decision-support depth at MATE.
Dr. Sándor Takács

MATE grants the project rights and access to the 2022-2026 processing-tomato archive for the approved scientific purposes of FIELDWISE, with experimental metadata, under institutional data-use conditions to be documented before the action starts.

КРУМАТИК ЕООД (EIK 201511899, established 2011, Sofia), with signatory Lyubomir Lyubomirov Krumov, provides continuous software development from project start (DrR prototype, crop-configurable architecture, MVP migration) and later Bulgarian dissemination, distinct from AgroVIR's evaluation role.
SME

Krumatic's prior involvement in deploying the AgroVIR farm-management platform in Bulgaria is a commercial-deployment relationship, stated openly; no ownership, employment or family relationship between Krumatic and the fellow or another partner is known.

WP3 prospective validation uses an independent commercial farmer site in Hungary secured through the fellow's professional relationship; FIELDWISE installs a meteorological station and soil sensors and retains all specialised scientific measurements, while the farmer provides the field and routine management; the site is independent of the historical MATE experiments.

The independent commercial farmer provides written field access: site availability for the validation season(s) within M4-M18, permission for sensor installation (automated meteorological station, soil sensors), field measurements and UAV campaigns, agreed irrigation-treatment implementation, and routine crop management responsibilities.
The Szentendre Skanzen model-garden route is a contingency-only validation option subject to formal agreement and scientific suitability.

Институт по зеленчукови култури „Марица“ – Пловдив (Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute, Bulgarian Agricultural Academy; director Prof. Daniela Ganeva) is a post-MSCA replication/recalibration/extension route on no work-package month line and with no in-action effort.
